title: Onboard Asteria-70b v1.0: metadata, perf profiles, and changelog automation
author: Leah Park
body:
Motivation: Add Asteria-70b v1.0 to the model registry with curated metadata, canonical performance profiles for Redwood serving, and automated changelog/release notes generation. This PR centralizes onboarding artifacts required for Dedicated and Hosted catalog rollout and wires up the changelog automation so product/docs teams receive release notes on publish.

What changed: Added model metadata JSON, performance profile YAML tuned for typical LLM-completion workloads (seq_len distribution and batching knobs), an entry in the registry index, a docs page, unit tests for profile validation, and a small automation config that extracts changelog fragments from the model metadata and publishes them to the release-notes pipeline.

Files of interest: models/asteria/metadata.json, perf/profiles/asteria-70b-v1.yaml, docs/models/asteria.md, tools/changelog-generator/config.yaml, scripts/register_model.py, tests/perf/test_asteria_profiles.py.

Checklist: [x] Metadata schema populated (name, version, architecture, tokenizer, weights_url, license, tags) [x] Performance profiles for 8k/4k/2k context distributions [x] Profile validation tests run locally and in CI [x] Changelog automation config added and smoke-tested against staging pipeline [x] Docs page drafted with usage notes and suggested quantization profiles.

Testing and validation: Perf profiles validated against the perf harness (see test_asteria_profiles.py); profiles are parameterized for sequence-length mix we observed in internal telemetry for generative completion workloads. Changelog automation was connected to the staging release-notes pipeline and produced the expected fragment; CI run includes unit tests and the redwood-perf-lab smoke job which completed successfully.

Rollout plan: Merge to main will create registry entry gated by an internal policy to advertise the model in the hosted catalog. For Dedicated customers, ops will be notified to pull the metadata and associated artifact hashes. We will monitor token-level latency and cost for the first 48 hours using the perf canary dashboards and set a rollback window of 72 hours if regression is detected.

Backward compatibility: No breaking changes to registry schema; optional fields were added but defaults are provided.

Notes: This PR also normalizes perf profile keys to the new naming convention (cpu_batch_target -> batch_cpu_target) - the server runtime already supports both but the change simplifies downstream automation.

review_comments: Carlos Mendes: Left a couple nits on the profile thresholds - please justify CPU batch targets with perf numbers (addressed in commit a1b2c3d).
Aisha Rahman: Changelog hook looks good, can we add a smoke test to ensure fragments are published? (added smoke job in ci/redwood-perf-lab.yml).
Tomoko Saito: Verified metadata fields and license text; approved pending CI.
Leah Park (author): Responded to nits and pushed fixes; added a short note in the docs explaining the batch_normalizer.
CI Bot: All checks passed after rerun.
release_notes:
- Onboarded Asteria-70b v1.0 to the model registry with curated metadata.
- Added canonical performance profiles (8k/4k/2k) and validation tests.
- Automated changelog fragment generation for model releases.
- Docs page with usage notes and recommended quantization profiles.
